approachQuestion.prompt: A sensor session begins with an empty collection. Its immutable list has n commands, 0 <= n <= 200,000. INSERT(x) adds a signed 64-bit reading as the newest entry. REMOVE discards the newest entry, doing nothing when empty. LOW reports the minimum of all current entries, or the distinguished symbol EMPTY when none exist. Return all LOW reports in order. Duplicate readings are separate entries. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total processing time over the list. Input: [INSERT(8),INSERT(3),INSERT(3),REMOVE,LOW,REMOVE,LOW]. Output: [3,8].

options.text: Store each inserted reading with the minimum from the bottom through that entry. REMOVE pops one pair; LOW reads the top minimum or EMPTY.
options.feedback: Each saved minimum describes the exact prefix restored after a pop, including duplicate minima.

options.text: Keep readings in a stack and one minimum scalar; update it on INSERT but leave it unchanged on REMOVE.
options.feedback: [INSERT(8),INSERT(3),REMOVE,LOW] must report 8, but the retained scalar reports 3.

options.text: Keep a reading stack plus a stack of strictly decreasing minima, without counts. Push a minimum only when strictly smaller; on removing a reading equal to the current minimum, pop that minimum.
options.feedback: Two equal minima need multiplicity. In the given example, removing one 3 discards the only record of 3 even though another remains.

options.text: Keep readings in a stack. For every LOW, scan all active readings to find the minimum, or report EMPTY.
options.feedback: This is correct and preserves removal order, but repeated LOW commands rescan an unchanged prefix; saving its minimum avoids that cost.

feedback.reason: Removing the newest entry restores an earlier prefix, whose minimum can be saved with that entry.
details: On INSERT, push the reading and the lesser of that reading and the previous top minimum. Pop one pair on REMOVE when nonempty. LOW returns the top saved minimum, or EMPTY.

Store the minimum alongside each pushed reading so removing the top reveals the earlier minimum immediately. Duplicate minima need separate saved states; removing one minimum must not forget another still present.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For annotated-minimum-stack, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The input is immutable and excluded from auxiliary space. Returned output is excluded, but all working buffers count even if later copied into output.
Fixed-size integers, characters, indices and comparisons take constant time. Arithmetic is unit cost under the stated range guarantee.
Use an iterative implementation with a preallocated n-entry array and a top index: push and pop take constant time. No recursion, hashing, or hidden whole-buffer copies occur.
Materializing output takes time proportional to its length; no persistent snapshots or string concatenation are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each command updates one value/minimum pair at the stack top.
details: Every command uses constant work and each LOW writes one report. An all-INSERT list retains n fixed-size pairs. Output copying costs at most linear time; output exclusion does not remove the pair stack. Time and auxiliary space are O(n).
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: n INSERT commands leave n reading/minimum pairs in the working stack; report exclusion does not exclude those pairs.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: LOW reads a saved minimum directly, and REMOVE reveals the previous saved minimum without rescanning all readings.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A full successful command stream can require inspecting every command and emitting every LOW report.
